The total resistance of the loop is r + R1 + R2 = 1Ω + 3Ω + 2Ω = 6Ω, and the current I = E/(r + R1 + R2) = 12V/6Ω = 2A. The voltage across C1 is the potential difference from the middle node of R1-R2 to the right main conducting wire, namely the voltage drop across R2: U1 = IR2 = 2A × 2Ω = 4V. The voltage across C2 is the potential difference from the left main conducting wire to the lower node/right main conducting wire, namely the terminal voltage of the external circuit: U2 = I(R1 + R2) = 2A × 5Ω = 10V. Thus Q1 = C1U1 = 4μF × 4V = 16μC, Q2 = C2U2 = 1μF × 10V = 10μC, so Q1:Q2 = 16:10 = 8:5.
